verdict.rationale: Flagsmith documents a self-hosted Edge Proxy that runs the Flagsmith Engine inside your own infrastructure. Server-side SDKs connect to it, which keeps SDK traffic in-network, and it acts as a local cache that serves requests without hitting the Core API. However, no evidence explicitly says flags keep being served when the vendor is unreachable, and only server-side SDKs are named. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of serving flags during a vendor outage (failover and staleness behavior), client-side SDK support through the proxy, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a platform engineer, I can run a relay/edge proxy so flags stay served when the vendor is unreachable and SDK traffic stays inside my network

citations.quote: The Flagsmith Edge Proxy is a service that you host yourself, that allows you to run an instance of the Flagsmith Engine close to your servers.
Run the Edge Proxy within in your own infrastructure and connect to it from your server-side SDKs
The proxy also acts as a local cache, allowing you to make requests to the proxy without hitting the Core API.
